title: Protein and mRNA Expression Profiles of Soft Tissue Sarcomas
summary:
This study analyses tissue samples from soft-tissue tumours in order to better understand how soft-tissue sarcomas are characterised at the level of proteins and messenger RNA (mRNA). The study includes patients presenting with a soft-tissue tumour of initially indeterminate nature, for whom a tissue sample (core needle biopsy) is medically required in any case to clarify the diagnosis. Whether a tumour is benign or malignant only becomes apparent after histological examination; benign findings may therefore remain within the study as a comparison group.

During the same procedure, a single additional tissue core is obtained solely for research, in addition to the cores required for diagnosis. Taking part in the study does not change the routine diagnostic work-up or the subsequent treatment. The additional sampling only slightly extends the procedure that is required in any case; possible risks correspond in particular to the general risks of a core needle biopsy, such as bleeding, infection or local discomfort. Participants derive no direct personal benefit from taking part.

The additional sample is stored frozen and used exclusively for the research question of this study. In the laboratory, various proteins and mRNA are measured and linked to the corresponding pseudonymised clinical and histopathological information. The aim is not to establish a diagnosis in individual participants – this is done independently of the study – but to gain general insights into the differences between and the development of various soft-tissue tumours by comparing many samples.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other connective and soft tissue

interventions.name: Single-arm study cohort: Patients with a soft-tissue tumour of indeterminate dignity for whom a core needle biopsy is indicated to establish the diagnosis are included. During the biopsy that is planned in any case, a single, exclusively study-specific tissue core is obtained in addition to the core

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a soft-tissue tumour of unclear or indeterminate dignity for whom a core needle biopsy is the diagnostic method of choice and who consent to it. Histological classification (malignant, intermediate or benign) is only established after enrolment; all cases enrolled in this way – including findings that turn out to be histologically benign – generally remain in the study cohort as a comparison group.
Age between 18 and 90 years
Capacity to consent and written informed consent provided
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 18 years
Lack of capacity to consent (e.g. psychiatric impairment, mechanical ventilation, persons under legal guardianship)
Concomitant conditions with potential confounding influence, in particular autoimmune diseases and concurrent malignancies other than soft-tissue sarcomas
Difficult-to-access tumours that must be secured by incisional biopsy as a last resort
Retroperitoneal or intrathoracic tumours
Vascular malformations
Lesions smaller than 1.5 cm
